//: WHY AN APK IS TWICE THE SIZE OF WHAT THE PLAY STORE SENDS.
An Android phone runs one of four instruction sets. A plain APK has to
work on any of them, so it carries the React Native engine four times
over - arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86 and x86_64 - and only one of those
copies is ever run. That is the 104 MB.
An app bundle (.aab) sends Google all four and Google builds a private
APK per phone with only its own copy inside. That download is roughly a
third of the size. A competitor's '54 MB' on the store listing is that
figure; comparing it with our sideload APK is not comparing like with
So: 'production' stays an app bundle, which is what goes on the store.
'preview' is the APK for sending to a shopkeeper by WhatsApp, and it now
drops the two x86 builds - those are emulators and a few Chromebooks, not
phones - which takes about 40% off it at no cost to any real customer.
'universal' is kept for the rare machine that needs x86.
